page: Microsoft Azure F16ams_v6 is a virtual machine configuration designed for memory-intensive and compute-focused enterprise workloads. Powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance runs on the x86_64 architecture using an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. The configuration provisions 16 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.7 GHz with a single thread per core, backed by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates vector instruction extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, as well as hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI.

Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB of RAM, establishing an elevated ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Synthetic evaluations reflect this capacity with a PassMark memory score of 2,777.71, positioning the instance in the top 25 percent of tested systems. Cache-level memory read bandwidth reaches 2,376.32 GB/sec for small blocks, while uncached large-block operations maintain 75.42 GB/sec read and 56.18 GB/sec write throughput. The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring remote persistent disks for filesystem operations, and does not provide an integrated GPU accelerator.

Benchmark outcomes show distinct performance profiles across varying computational patterns. Single-threaded execution is particularly robust, achieving a stress-ng single-core score of 3,078.78 (top 25 percent). In lightweight language model processing, it reaches top-tier throughput of 342.9 tokens/sec for text generation on a 135M model, tapering to 16.22 tokens/sec when handling 7B parameter models. Multi-core compute performance and web serving capacity align with median cloud standards, demonstrated by 49,035.97 in stress-ng multi-core and 20.36 GB/sec in static web throughput.

From an operational and resource efficiency standpoint, the F16ams_v6 provides dedicated core execution combined with generous RAM allocation without the overhead of attached local disks. This architecture suits in-memory caching platforms such as Redis (tested at 38.11 million SET ops/sec), relational database hosting, intermediate data processing, and single-thread-sensitive computational batch tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure F16ams_v6 is a memory-enhanced compute instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 dedicated physical cores clocked at 3.7 GHz alongside 128.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a high 8.0 GB memory-to-core allocation. Hardware acceleration includes AVX-512 VNNI and BF16 instruction sets, though the instance omits bundled local storage and discrete GPUs, relying on remote volumes for persistence. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-quartile memory performance and strong single-core execution, demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core metric of 3,078.78 and 342.9 tokens/sec on lightweight text generation models. Multi-threaded compute, static web serving (20.36 GB/sec), and database transactions deliver steady median-tier throughput. The system is structurally engineered for memory-heavy enterprise deployments, including Redis caching clusters, relational database management systems, and specialized data engineering pipelines.
